What an incredibly hilarious yet knife-sharp talk on one of the most plaguing frustrations of life. Procrastination is something that I have struggled with for a long time, but has completely taken hold of my life for about the last 6 years. "Long-term procrastination has made them feel like a spectator in their own lives" 12:24 . That hit like a punch in the gut. Increasing feelings of shame, regret, etc., with each failed-to-complete task have left me feeling stuck in various areas of life. It has often felt like being a passenger in a car driving past a wreck; helpless yet unable to look away. That instant gratification monkey just won't get off my back. The Life Calendar was a harsh wake-up call. There feel like not enough boxes to encompass a human life, and yet many aren't even promised 90 years. How many boxes do any of us truly have, and how many- if any- should be wasted? If long-term procrastination is procrastination without a deadline, then long-term procrastination does not truly exist. In life, there is one final unknown deadline to every task we have: death. Instead of living as if this deadline does not exist, maybe we should live as if things are always due next week, since we're not even promised tomorrow.

Tim Urban, a writer and blogger, shares his personal struggle with procrastination and offers insights into the minds of procrastinators (2:56). Here's a breakdown of his key points: The Procrastinator's Brain (3:16): Urban illustrates the procrastinator's brain with two main characters: the Rational Decision Maker and the Instant Gratification Monkey. The monkey, driven by easy and fun activities, often hijacks the wheel, leading to unproductive tangents like reading Wikipedia or watching YouTube videos (4:01). The Dark Playground (6:44): This is the space where procrastinators engage in leisure activities when they should be working. It's a place filled with guilt, dread, and anxiety because the fun is unearned. The Panic Monster (7:19): This "guardian angel" is dormant until a deadline approaches, or public embarrassment is imminent. The Panic Monster is the only thing the Instant Gratification Monkey fears, forcing the procrastinator to finally get things done. Urban recounts his own experience writing a 90-page thesis in 72 hours and preparing for his TED Talk (1:55, 8:23). Two Kinds of Procrastination (10:56): Deadline-based procrastination: The Panic Monster ensures tasks are eventually completed, containing the negative effects to the short term. Non-deadline procrastination: This type occurs when there's no immediate deadline, such as pursuing career goals, maintaining relationships, or taking care of one's health. Without the Panic Monster, the procrastination extends indefinitely, leading to long-term unhappiness and regret (11:56). A Call to Action (12:41): Urban concludes by showing a "life calendar" to emphasize the limited time we have. He urges everyone to recognize their own procrastination, especially in non-deadline situations, and to start working on important things today, or "sometime soon" (13:06).

I see a lot of people face the same problems in this comment section but I would like to share some Good news. But first I will start with the bad news. The bad news is that due to our ancestors disobedience to God sin had entered the world and before a righteous and holy God we were separated from Him because of our sinful nature which resulted in brokenness, guilt, and spiritual death. This is the Good news, God's love for us was and is so deep that he decided to send his only son Jesus Christ who is fully and fully God to pay the price that we could not pay as humans by living a perfect life here on earth and because the penalty for sin was death, Jesus went on the cross he took all of your sins and all of the sins of humanity, and He placed them upon Himself (1 Peter 2:24) and died for them. Even though he didn't deserve such a gruesome death, he loved us enough to die for us. He then raises from the dead three days later defeating sin and death forever. Now what does this mean for you? Jesus has accomplished what was necessary to remove the barrier between you and God, He offers salvation to you as a gift (Ephesians 2:8). As a gift, that means there is nothing you can do to earn it. However, just like any gift, you have to receive it. You can receive Jesus's free gift by believing in your heart and confessing with your mouth that Jesus Christ is Lord. (Eph. 2:8-9, John 3:16). When you place your faith in Jesus to be your Savior, He rescues you. He applies the forgiveness that He purchased for you on the cross to your life and reconciles you to God. The moment you put your faith in Jesus for salvation, the Holy Spirit comes to dwell in you (Ephesians 1:13) and you enter into a spiritual union with Jesus (Galatians 2:20). Jesus will set you free from the bondages of sin and death. There is no shame or condemnation in Christ Jesus for he will wash you in his blood and make you a new creation in Christ Jesus.
